entities.description: Customer. The same entity is physically stored in three databases under different primary keys. The link between them is not a real foreign key, because PostgreSQL has no cross-database constraints.

keys.note: The table's own primary key is order_id; customer_id (bigint) references crm.customer.customer_id.
The canonical customer record, kept in the CRM.
bigint, nullable: not every customer has a billing account. References billing.account.account_id.

notes: PostgreSQL cannot JOIN across databases, even on the same server. Do it in two `query` calls — collect the ids in one database, pass them to the other as a parameter (`= ANY($1)`) — or in a single `federated_lookup` call. `connection` here names a connection without its environment suffix: one map serves every environment, and an id ending in a suffix listed in PGSTEWARD_ENV_SUFFIXES finds the entry written without it, so use whichever suffixed connection you actually have.
